questions.prompt: A call with strike $100 costs $10.45 and the put with the same strike and expiry costs $5.57. What does the straddle cost?
questions.explanation: A straddle is a call and a put with the same strike and expiry, so it costs 10.45 + 5.57 = $16.02.

questions.prompt: You sell a straddle priced at 20% implied volatility and delta hedge it daily. The stock moves at 16%. What happens on average in the simulation?
questions.explanation: The stock moved less than the 20% in the price, so the hedged seller earned $3.09 on average. That gain is the volatility risk premium at work.

questions.prompt: Nine quiet years earn $27.81 and one crash year loses $15.63. Why does this make sizing so important for a volatility seller?
options: Because one crash year erases about five quiet years, and too much leverage can wipe out the account first
Because the premium is paid only in crash years
Because realised volatility is always above implied volatility
questions.explanation: 15.63 / 3.09 is about 5, so one crash wipes out five quiet years. A seller with too much leverage may not survive the crash to collect the later years.
